title: fix(components): a tabs item draws its panel from `content` only (objectui#9590)
body:
Part of #9590
Clause-②: no — no declared surface widens; an undeclared item-level read and the texts that teach it are retired

This PR lands the `tabs` half of objectui#9590. It must not close the card: the `list` half is handed back to the seat as a decision (see "Why `Part of`" below).

## What changed

- `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/tabs.tsx`: each panel draws `renderChildren(item.content)`. The `(item as any).body` fallback is gone. `TabItem` declares no `body` on either published face: `TabItemSchema` requires `content` and strips `body`. The fallback honoured a key the contract refuses, which is the lenient-fallback shape AGENTS.md #0.1 bans.
- New pin `tabs-item-body-retired-9590.test.tsx`: `subject` (an item with `body` alone paints nothing from it), `control` (a `content` item paints), and `precedence` (`content` beside `body` paints `content` only).
- `tabs-default-items-parse-9941.test.tsx`: its `controlB.equality` row read the retired arm, and its own comment said it would retire with the arm. It is removed, and the header is re-scoped. No subject row moved.
- `scripts/__tests__/body-dialect-census.test.ts`: the objectui#9590 pointer gets a dated note. The `tabs` read is retired, the `dashboard` key stopped being taught under objectui#8290, and `list`'s read is unchanged at this change.
- `.changeset/6771-retire-body-child-list-dialect.md`: the item-level bullet is scoped "At this change", and gets a dated note for its `tabs` half. The frontmatter is byte-identical: md5 `822a2503a99c3201bf24704364f590cc` before and after.
- `.changeset/9590-tabs-item-content-only.md`: `@object-ui/components` `minor`, because a published read is retired.

## Re-pricing (the question comment 5728393376 requires)

The answer is simpler for two subjects and harder for one. Every reading below was taken on base `bc97f9247`.

| subject | reading | verdict |
|:--|:--|:--|
| `tabs` item `body` | producer scan (`pnpm census:body-dialect-producers`): 0 producers. The lit control is the same scan over the `packages/components/src` tree at `1db82373f`, before objectui#9941, which answers 3 item producers in `tabs.tsx` `defaultProps`. Zod door: a `body`-only tab item is REFUSED (`invalid_type` at `items.0.content`), and `body` beside `content` is stripped. | simpler: dead fallback, retired here |
| `dashboard` widget `body` | already discharged on main. PR objectui#10452 (card objectui#8290, `ab50ccc12`) rewrote the `schema-reference.md` rows and prose. The plugin-dashboard README already says "no nested `body` slot". `DashboardWidgetSchema` is `.strict()` and refuses `body`. The `packages/plugin-dashboard/src` source has no widget `body` read (the only `.body` hit is `document.body.appendChild`). | premise gone, no edit |
| `list` `items[].body` | JSON/MD walker over every tracked `.json` and every fenced block in `.md`/`.mdx` at base: 11 `list` items, and exactly 1 carries `body`. That one is the published skill `skills/objectui/guides/schema-expressions.md` (its `os:check` example), and it is also the walker's lit control. Zod door: a `body`-only list item parses GREEN as `{}`, so `body` is silently stripped. Render probe (scratch, not committed): `body` renders its node; a node-valued `content`, the DECLARED `ListItem.content` type, fails with `Component "list" failed to render` / `Objects are not valid as a React child`. | harder: see below |

objectstack `origin/main` `16c5a33`, same walker, reading from the ref for both enumeration and content: 0 `list` items, 0 `tabs` items with `body`, 0 `dashboard` widgets with `body`.

H2, the conversion: `@objectstack/spec`'s conversion registry has no entry for a `list` or `tabs` item. It cannot have one either: `PageComponentType` does not model the bare `list`/`tabs` registrations, which reach a page only through its open string arm. The objectui#6771 precedent retired objectui-only reads on a liveness reading, with no spec conversion. ⇒ no conversion is owed for the `tabs` read, and none exists for `list`.

## Why `Part of`: the `list` half is a decision, not an edit

- `body` is `list`'s only working node channel today. Retiring it means `list.tsx` must draw `renderChildren(item.content)` so that the declared `content` type renders. That makes it a behaviour change, not just a deletion.
- It falsifies published text outside this claim's file surface. The first is the published skill `skills/objectui/guides/schema-expressions.md`, which teaches `body` as `list`'s only `SchemaRenderer` channel (table row, prose, an `os:check` example). That file is a governed surface, and this PR is NOT governed today. The second is `packages/types` prose: the `ListSchema` `body`/`children` docblocks and the two `ListSchema` tombstone messages in `data-display.zod.ts`, which quote `item.content || renderChildren(item.body)`. The dispatch forbids `packages/types` edits.
- The claim says to stop on a surface breach, so `list.tsx` is untouched. The options, analysed on the four axes, are in the dev report on the card.

## Acceptance notes (observed, not filed)

- `packages/types/src/__tests__/content-channel-family-d-9256.test.ts`: the `tabs` LIVE CONTROL comment still quotes `item.content || (item as any).body`. It is a test comment, left alone because the dispatch forbids `packages/types` edits. The `list` round touches the same file's `list` comments anyway. Carrier: the next objectui#9590 round.
- `content/docs/components/layout/tabs.mdx` and `content/docs/components/data-display/list.mdx` show `interface` sketches that drift from `TabsSchema`/`ListSchema` (for example `defaultValue?: number`, `items: SchemaNode[]`). This is drift, not a failing example.
